touches.subject: Your paralegal opening, and a faster way to fill it
touches.body:
Hi Dana,

Your paralegal post has been up since 28 August. When a seat stays open
that long it's usually the local market rather than the offer, and another
month of the same search rarely changes it.

We place trained legal staff with personal injury firms: one person,
dedicated to your cases, working inside Filevine. Not a pooled service desk,
and not a temp.

Every candidate is pre-vetted and trained on firm work before you meet
them. Interviewing costs nothing, and someone who fits can start in under
three days.

If it would help, I'll send two profiles matched to that seat. No
obligation either way.

Best regards,
Legal Soft — legalsoft.com

--
Reply with the word stop and I won't write to you again.

touches.subject: Re: your paralegal opening, the part that's usually stuck
touches.body:
Hi Dana,

One thing I should have said in my last note.

The part most personal injury firms hand over first isn't the paralegal
seat itself. It's the records chase: provider requests, the fourth call to
the same clinic, and the follow-up nobody has time to send before the week
ends.

If that's the part that's actually stuck, I can introduce two people who
do exactly that work all day. Interviewing costs nothing, and you keep the
profiles whether or not you hire.

Would that be useful?

Best regards,
Legal Soft — legalsoft.com

Reply with the word stop and I won't write to you again.

touches.subject: The unbilled hours between you and the fee
touches.body:
Hi Dana,

A different angle on the same thing.

On contingency, every hour your team spends chasing records is unbilled,
and it sits between you and the fee. A demand writer isn't a saving. It
shortens the gap to settlement, which is a different argument entirely,
and the reason personal injury firms are usually the easiest version of
this conversation.

If it's worth ten minutes, I'll walk you through how those numbers tend to
look at a firm your size.

Best regards,
Legal Soft — legalsoft.com

mentioning.
